jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.

ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.

We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

About the Role

Valon is deploying ValonOS, an AI‑native operating system for complex, regulated operations, with a high‑touch implementation model that pairs great software with world‑class on‑the‑ground execution. As an Implementation Manager, you keep complex, multi‑stakeholder programs moving with clarity, pace, and trust. You are the client’s primary day‑to‑day partner and the internal conductor who aligns Deployment Strategy, Forward‑Deployed Engineering, Product, and Operations to deliver outcomes quickly and safely.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the plan of record for an enterprise deployment

    Keep track of all tasks, risks, issues, and open items across different work areas. Surface critical path, dependencies, and decision needs with precision.

  • Drive execution to timeline

    Anticipate long‑lead blockers, assign DRIs, set clear timelines, and burn down risks. Balance speed with quality in regulated, legacy environments.

  • Be the main client touchpoint

    Build trusted relationships with project manager counterparts and business leaders. Read the room, manage expectations, and translate feedback into crisp actions.

  • Orchestrate cross‑functional teams

    Coordinate Deployment Strategists, Forward Deployed Engineers, Engineering, Product, and Analytics from discovery through go live.

  • Manage scope and change

    Capture requests, cluster themes, and route to the minimum viable path. Use off‑the‑shelf assets and sessions to avoid bespoke work where possible.

  • Land enablement and adoption

    Plan and run training, comms, and readiness for target user cohorts. Track adoption against thresholds and close gaps.

  • Run executive cadence

    Prepare materials and drive steering forums with client executives. Keep decisions, risks, and value tracking transparent and on‑track.

  • Contribute to the playbook

    Codify templates, checklists, and talk tracks that make future deployments faster and more repeatable.

What Success Looks Like

  • Clear, living plan of record with no surprises on critical path.

  • Risks and dependencies surfaced early and burned down proactively.

  • Transition completed smoothly with minimal business disruption and contingency plans ready but not needed.

  • Client stakeholders trust the program and feel well‑managed; decisions made to cadence.

  • Adoption targets achieved with trained users and a stable support model.

  • Minimal bespoke build through smart expectation‑setting and strong use of existing assets.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years in implementation management, consulting, program management, or similar roles driving complex enterprise rollouts.

  • Exceptional organization and written/verbal communication. Operate with clarity in ambiguity and high‑stakes settings.

  • Relationship builder with high EQ who earns trusted‑advisor status with counterparts and executives.

  • Strong judgment on when to escalate, when to say no, and how to scope to the minimum viable path.

  • Comfortable coordinating across multiple vendors and stakeholders in complex, compliance‑sensitive environments.

Preferred Backgrounds

  • Experience in implementation management, consulting, investment banking, private equity, hedge funds, or enterprise software deployment where you managed cross‑functional workstreams under tight timelines.

  • Background in forward‑deployed work with product or engineering teams.

  • Fluency with program tools like Notion, Google Workspace, and project/issue trackers.

Work Environment

  • This is a full-remote role but can be hybrid in our NY or SF offices

  • High‑ownership environment with small, senior teams.

  • Expected travel ~10% to client sites and key working sessions, flexing up around milestones.

How We Work

  • Small, high‑trust teams where ownership beats ceremony.

  • We treat implementation as 50% of the product: success = software + deployment.

  • Builders over coordinators. You own outcomes, not just tasks.

Why Valon

  • Proven in the real world. ValonOS is battle‑tested in live operations, so you’re not pushing a slide‑ware roadmap — you’re deploying capabilities that already deliver value.

  • Build with elite partners. You’ll work shoulder‑to‑shoulder with former founders, ex‑FAANG engineers, and consultants who prize ownership and pace over ceremony.

  • Direct line to impact. Your programs unlock measurable P&L outcomes for customers — faster time‑to‑value, lower cost to operate, better customer experience — and those wins shape our product roadmap.

  • High‑trust autonomy. Small, senior teams with clear goals. You’ll make the calls, run the room, and ship. We optimize for leverage, not meetings.

  • Career compounder. The role blends executive customer exposure, complex transformation, and product influence — a rare mix that compounds your judgment and scope.

  • Momentum and market pull. Legacy transformations are inevitable; our AI‑native approach lets enterprises leapfrog, not inch forward. You’ll be at the tip of that spear.

Benefits

  • Compensation: competitive salary with a meaningful stake in the company via equity, and 401(k) plan. The base salary range reflects multiple levels. We assess level based on a combination of experience and interview performance.

  • Health & well-being: we’ll invest in your physical and mental well-being with comprehensive medical, dental, & vision benefits.

  • Free Food: daily lunch, and dinner provided through Forkable for in-office team members.

  • Commuter benefits: pre-tax deductions for public transit, rideshares, and parking to simplify your daily commute.

  • Grow together: company wide orientation for you to successfully onboard and other learning & development opportunities including regular review cycles that feature 360-degree feedback.

  • Play together: quarterly budgets for team and company outings. Use it for team swag, cooking classes, or team dinners.

  • Generous time off: flexible paid time off with no annual limit, sick days, and 11 company holidays.

  • Baby bonding time: 12 weeks of fully paid leave for both birthing and non-birthing parents, so you can spend uninterrupted time welcoming and caring for your newest family member.

Throughout the interview process, please remember that emails will only be from valon.com email addresses. We will never ask for any personally identifiable information during the interview process itself. Please reach out to talent@valon.com if you have any requests to verify the authenticity of an outreach.

Valon is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Valon makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

About the Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

About the Team

You’ll join the core Platform & Infrastructure product org. This team builds the foundational systems and services that serve as the backbone for features across our entire product suite.

While many infrastructure teams operate behind the scenes, ours sits at an intersection. We build systems that internal vertical teams depend on, and we also deliver features that directly touch end users (e.g. platforms, self-service tools, dashboards). Because of that, you’ll balance deep technical rigor with customer empathy.

We operate in a high-growth, high-authenticity engineering culture. You’ll partner with senior engineers, architects, and cross-functional leads, and have high visibility across the org.

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, Infrastructure & Platform, you will:

  • Define and own the roadmap for one or more core infrastructure domains (such as notification platform, documents platform, user management, etc.)

  • Deeply engage with internal stakeholders (engineering leads, vertical PMs, operations) and our customers to drive discovery and specification

  • Drive initiatives end-to-end: from ideation, discovery, scoping, to launch, adoption, and iteration

  • Work directly with customers/stakeholders (sometimes on-site at their operations) so that your deliverables are finely tuned to their unique and complex processes

  • Ensure infrastructure is resilient, scalable, observable, and secure — balancing performance, reliability, and long-term extensibility

  • Lead discovery for complex customer processes: conduct customer interviews and complete process mapping across multiple customers of varying profiles

  • Deep ability to map processes and systems even in high ambiguity — e.g. you can take a domain with many moving pieces and build a reliable abstraction

  • Write clear, structured product specs, user stories that are easy to understand, even for someone without any domain knowledge

  • Partner closely with engineering leadership and architects to make tradeoffs on design, performance, scale, and technical debt

  • Evangelize infrastructure best practices across the organization and influence roadmap tradeoffs

Ideal Background

  • 5+ years of product management (or equivalent) experience, ideally with exposure to b2b saas products, product infrastructure, and platforms

  • Strong technical fluency: experience working with engineers around systems, APIs, data models, etc.

  • Excellent customer discovery skills: comfortable conducting interviews, writing journey maps, and synthesizing qualitative + quantitative inputs

  • Track record of shipping infrastructure or platform features that were adopted broadly or had measurable impact

  • Highly structured thinker, able to write and communicate complex concepts simply

  • Comfortable operating with high autonomy, ambiguity, and responsibility

  • Strong collaboration skills: able to manage stakeholders, drive alignment, and hold cross-team accountability

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, or a closely related field

Why Join Valon?

  • Transform a $13 trillion industry by building the operating system for mortgage servicing, replacing 40-year-old legacy systems with modern, AI-powered infrastructure

  • Join at a pivotal moment: We're rapidly scaling, with contracts signed or in negotiation representing nearly 30% of the entire mortgage servicing market

  • Work on complex, high-impact problems with massive scale, our platform will power servicing operations for millions of homeowners across the country

  • Product and Engineering-led culture with exceptional talent density, work alongside world-class engineers and product leaders who value velocity, clarity, and deep technical excellence

  • Real product ownership with enterprise impact: your decisions will directly influence how major financial institutions operate and serve their customers

  • Unique market position: We're winning against entrenched incumbents by delivering 75%+ cost reduction and a modern software experience that were previously not possible

Benefits

  • Compensation: competitive salary with a meaningful stake in the company via equity, and 401(k) plan. The base salary range reflects multiple levels. We assess level based on a combination of experience and interview performance.

  • Health & well-being: we’ll invest in your physical and mental well-being with comprehensive medical, dental, & vision benefits.

  • Free Food: daily lunch, and dinner provided through Forkable for in-office team members.

  • Commuter benefits: pre-tax deductions for public transit, rideshares, and parking to simplify your daily commute.

  • Grow together: company wide orientation for you to successfully onboard and other learning & development opportunities including regular review cycles that feature 360-degree feedback.

  • Play together: quarterly budgets for team and company outings. Use it for team swag, cooking classes, or team dinners.

  • Generous time off: flexible paid time off with no annual limit, sick days, and 11 company holidays.

  • Baby bonding time: 12 weeks of fully paid leave for both birthing and non-birthing parents, so you can spend uninterrupted time welcoming and caring for your newest family member.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.

ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.

We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

What this role is

Deployment Strategists own live enterprise deployments of ValonOS: part operator, part product strategist, part data investigator, and part executive translator. You diagnose how a regulated servicing operation works, decide what needs to change, configure the solution, and stay accountable until client operators are live and the business outcome is measurable.

The job is not to make recommendations from the outside. The job is to figure out what is true, make the right call under ambiguity, and drive the work until the outcome exists in the real world.

Why Valon

How many times in your career are you going to get the chance to deploy an eight- or nine-figure software contract into one of the most regulated industries on the planet?

Not many. That's what we do here.

Valon is the AI-native operating system for mortgage servicing - a $13 trillion industry running on infrastructure built before the iPhone. We did not try to fix it from the outside. We bought our way in: built and operate our own mortgage servicing business managing $110B+ in loans, used that operation to deeply understand every workflow that breaks at scale, and then built the software we wished existed.

The result: a 0% margin business turned 60%+. Our own servicing operation runs at 4x the employee efficiency of the industry. Major enterprise servicers - including Newrez - are now deploying ValonOS across the industry. The contracts we are rolling out are some of the largest and most complex enterprise software deployments anywhere in financial services right now.

Deployment Strategists are the people who make those rollouts actually work.

 

Why mortgage servicing is the most interesting problem you've (probably) never thought about

Every monthly payment from a homeowner triggers a chain reaction: money has to move, accounting entries have to balance, escrow has to disburse to the right counties and insurers, and every step has to satisfy regulators across all 50 states - each with its own foreclosure rules, notice timelines, fee restrictions, and licensing regimes. Get any of it wrong and you have created a CFPB headline.

Now do that for millions of loans, with hundreds of legacy vendors, dozens of capital partners, and operators who have been doing it one way for 30 years.

Mortgage servicing has resisted software automation for decades not because the individual problems are unsolvable, but because the abstractions are so hard to model correctly that no one had done it. We did. It took six years. Now we are deploying it across the industry - and that is where you come in.

 

What you will do

A client recently described what we do as "open-heart surgery while the patient is still walking around running their business." That is accurate. You are handed a multi-decade-old operation processing hundreds of thousands of loans, with a reputation, a regulator, and a P&L - and you have to migrate it onto our platform without anything breaking. Under tight timelines. With executives watching.

A Deployment Strategist:

  • Maps a client's current operation, identifies the gaps to ValonOS, sequences the roadmap, and gets sign-off from leaders who have been doing this for 25 years.

  • Spends Tuesday querying the data warehouse to figure out whether a payoff event has actually occurred across our system, the servicer's ops, and a capital partner's books - and then drives a decision the business is willing to bet on.

  • Translates between groups that do not naturally talk to each other: engineering, the client's servicing operations team, capital partners, compliance, product, and executives.

  • Sits onsite watching foreclosure, escrow, loss mitigation, or cash operations specialists work, then comes back and helps rebuild the workflow.

  • Configures and deploys the solution, watches client operators actually use it, and stays accountable for whether the workflow produces the measurable business outcome.

  • Briefs everyone else. The DS does not get briefed. The work starts with raw data, raw code, and raw conversations, and ends in a decision the business commits to.

 

How we work

A few things we actually believe, not aspirationally:

  • You own the outcome, not the recommendation. This is the anti-consulting role. You do not hand off a deck and walk away. You configure, deploy, iterate, and measure the result. Our contracts are performance-based, so when your deployment works, Valon wins. Your work shows up in the P&L.

  • You figure it out. There will be incomplete data, undocumented legacy behavior, tense client tradeoffs, and unclear ownership. The job is to create clarity anyway.

  • You build alignment, but you do not hide behind consensus. You synthesize, recommend, commit, and defend the decision with evidence.

  • Code and data beat decks. A working query, a real workflow, a shipped change, or a clear operating decision wins over prettier slides.

  • AI fluency is how the work gets done, not a nice-to-have. Our team uses coding agents, builds custom skills, and develops an internal knowledge layer, DeploymentOS, that you will use and extend. Our highest performers do not just use these tools - they tell our engineers what to build next and ship workflows themselves when waiting would be too slow.

  • You are writing the playbook, not executing one. Every framework we use was built by someone in this seat figuring it out for the first time. The next versions will be written by you.

 

What success looks like

You are succeeding here if senior leaders trust you with ambiguous, high-stakes problems and feel the work is in safe hands.

That means:

  • You can walk into a domain you do not understand, build a working model quickly, find the data and people who matter, make a recommendation, and drive it to an operational outcome.

  • You move fast without becoming sloppy. You are energized by incomplete context, not paralyzed by it.

  • You can reason through a regulated operating system from first principles instead of relying on generic frameworks or waiting for a subject-matter expert to hand you the answer.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS

Deployment Strategy Leads own the people and the quality bar behind ValonOS deployments. You are a specialist in a deployment domain, and you build, coach, and hold accountable a team of 3-10 people. Deployment Strategists across the entire customer journey — from contract signature through go-live through adoption. You are part manager, part deployment operator, part quality control. The team's outcomes are your outcomes. The job is not to manage from a dashboard. You stay close enough to the work to catch problems before they become client-facing, and close enough to your people to know when they need a stretch, a course correction, or to be unblocked.

 


WHY VALON

How many times in your career are you going to get the chance to build and run a team deploying eight-and nine-figure software contracts into one of the most regulated industries on the planet? Not many. That's what we do here.

Valon is the AI-native operating system for mortgage servicing — a $13 trillion industry running on infrastructure built before the iPhone. We did not try to fix it from the outside. We bought our way in: built and operate our own mortgage servicing business managing $110B+ in loans, used that operation to deeply understand every workflow that breaks at scale, and then built the software we wished existed.

The result: a 0% margin business turned 60%+. Our own servicing operation runs at 4x the employee efficiency of the industry. Major enterprise servicers — including Newrez — are now deploying ValonOS across the industry. The contracts we are rolling out are some of the largest and most complex enterprise software deployments anywhere in financial services right now. Deployment Strategy Leads make sure the people running those rollouts get better every quarter, not just busier.

 


WHY MORTGAGE SERVICING IS THE MOST INTERESTING PROBLEM YOU'VE (PROBABLY) NEVER THOUGHT ABOUT

Every monthly payment from a homeowner triggers a chain reaction: money has to move, accounting entries have to balance, escrow has to disburse to the right counties and insurers, and every step has to satisfy regulators across all 50 states — each with its own foreclosure rules, notice timelines, fee restrictions, and licensing regimes. Get any of it wrong and you have created a CFPB headline.

Now do that for millions of loans, with hundreds of legacy vendors, dozens of capital partners, and operators who have been doing it one way for 30 years.

Mortgage servicing has resisted software automation for decades not because the individual problems are unsolvable, but because the abstractions are so hard to model correctly that no one had done it. We did. It took six years. Now we are deploying it across the industry — and your team is on point.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

A client recently described what we do as “open-heart surgery while the patient is still walking around running their business.” That is accurate. Your team is handed multi-decade-old operations processing hundreds of thousands of loans, with a reputation, a regulator, and a P&L on the line — and you have to make sure every deployment lands without anything breaking.



A Deployment Strategy Lead:

 - Owns a deployment domain end-to-end: builds specialist depth in a particular product surface, client function, or operational workflow, and is the standard-bearer for quality in that domain across every deployment it touches.

 - Manages and coaches 3-10 Deployment Strategists: runs the learning loop, sharpens their judgment on ambiguous problems, and knows when to let someone run and when to step in.

 - Stays accountable for the full customer journey, not just launch day: contract to go-live to adoption. A deployment that goes live but doesn't stick is not a win.

 - Stays close enough to the work to catch quality problems early — reviewing configurations, sitting in on client conversations, reading the data, not just the status updates.

 - Raises the bar on the team's craft: better decisions, faster learning loops, stronger client trust, sharper ICs.

 - Translates upward and outward: to senior client leaders who have been doing this for 25 years, to Valon's product and engineering teams, and to your own reports who need clarity, not just direction.

 - You figure it out. There will be incomplete data, undocumented legacy behavior, tense client tradeoffs, and unclear ownership — both in the deployments and in the team problems. The job is to create clarity anyway.

 - You build alignment, but you do not hide behind consensus. You synthesize, recommend, commit, and defend the decision with evidence, and you coach your team to do the same.

 - Code and data beat decks. A working query, a real workflow, a shipped change, or a clear operating decision wins over prettier slides — for you and for the people you manage.

 - AI fluency is how the work gets done, not a nice-to-have. Your team uses coding agents, builds custom skills, and develops DeploymentOS. Part of your job is making sure that fluency keeps compounding across your pod.

 - You are writing the playbook, not executing one. Every framework we use was built by someone figuring it out for the first time. You are responsible for the next versions, and for making sure your team's hard-won lessons don't die with the individual deployment.

 


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

You are succeeding here if senior leaders trust your domain and your team with ambiguous, high-stakes problems and feel the work is in safe hands.

That means:

 - Your deployments consistently land on time, on quality, and stick past go-live into real adoption.

 - Your Deployment Strategists get sharper because of you — clearer decisions, faster learning loops, better client trust, stronger individual judgment.

 - You can walk into a domain problem you don't fully understand, build a working model quickly, and know which of your reports to point at it and how to support them.

 - You move fast without becoming sloppy, and you keep your team moving fast without letting quality slip.

 - You can hold a room of senior client leaders and still go low-level enough to debug a workflow, query, data pipeline, or operating edge case yourself when it matters.

 - You know the difference between coaching someone through ambiguity and rescuing them from it, and you choose deliberately.

 - You have taught yourself new tools because the work demanded it, and you expect the same of your team.

 - You are comfortable being both a manager and extremely low-level in the same day.

 - You can communicate clearly with executives, operators, engineers, clients, and your own reports without changing the substance of your thinking.

 - You care about building a durable team and body of work, not just being near an interesting problem.

 


WHO MAY STRUGGLE HERE

We are direct about fit because the cost of a mismatch is high, for us and for you. This is probably not the right role if:

 - You are looking for a management lane focused on process and reporting rather than deployment outcomes and client adoption.

 - You prefer overseeing from a distance over staying close enough to the work to catch quality problems yourself.

 - You are uncomfortable with technical ambiguity, data messiness, or the tools (SQL, Python, AI agents) your team uses daily.

 - You want a role where people management and deployment ownership are neatly separated.

 - You are looking for generic enterprise SaaS management work. We are rebuilding the operating system

LOCATION AND TRAVEL

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.

ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.

We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

About the Role

Make the best builders in America understand that Valon is one of the most interesting places to work, and feel proud if they get in.

For six years, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer, proving that AI-native infrastructure could hold up in one of the country's most regulated, unforgiving environments, where getting it wrong has real consequences for real families. It held up. We turned a 0%-margin business into 60%+ margins while making it easier for families to pay their mortgages. In May 2026 we sold the servicer, and now we license the OS behind it.

That's the short version of a good story. Almost no one knows it yet.

We're hiring someone to fix that. You'll own Valon's external brand, starting with talent: how the company comes across to the engineers, operators, designers, and other builders we most want to hire. The job is equal parts strategy and writing, plus the judgment that connects them. You figure out what Valon's story should be and who it's for, decide what's worth saying, then say it well in whatever medium fits.

This isn't employer branding in the usual sense. There's no template and no agency to manage. You'll function as a high-impact IC running a small newsroom inside the company. You find the real stories, tell them so a person actually wants to read them, the place where they’re most likely to engage, and build a repeatable way to keep doing it.

Stripe made payments infrastructure feel like a generational mission. Anduril made a space engineers were avoiding feel like the most important work around. Valon's story is that big, and it's sitting there almost entirely untold. You'd be the first person to tell it properly.

Why brand-building here is the most interesting problem you've (probably) never thought about

Most communicators are torn between telling the mission story that attracts talent and investors and a more clinical marketing message for customers. We already know how to reach our customers, which means you get to focus solely on the talent brand (at least to start). You're writing for people making an identity decision, not a business transaction. The engineers are deciding what story they want to tell about this chapter of their life.

And while we're biased, we think the raw material here is pretty great. We've already built and outgrown one successful business (our mortgage servicer), and now we're taking on new industries. It's a substantive story, not a hype-y one (we're allergic to hype), and it's your job to convey the seriousness of our engineering story - building compliant, zero-downtime financial infrastructure - with heart, humor, and an allergy to spin.

What you'll do

Shape the story

Work out how to explain Valon clearly: what we're building, why it's hard, and why a strong candidate should care. Then build the material the rest of the company can reuse, including messaging for candidates and outside audiences, the specific stories and numbers that back it up, and clear answers to why people join.

Write the content

Get Valon in front of the people who form opinions about where to work:

  • Founder essays and posts, in the founders' voice

  • Company updates and longer memos

  • "Why I joined" and team stories

  • Product and technical stories written for a wider audience

  • Candidate-facing material that explains the company and the work

The skill is finding the best material already inside the company and writing it up so it reads like a person wrote it, not a press release.

Get other people talking

Owned content only goes so far. You should know the writers, podcasters, and newsletter authors who would find Valon genuinely interesting, build real relationships with them as humans, and pitch in a way that earns coverage rather than begs for it. The pitch is never "come cover our company." It's "here's an interesting thing happening in the world, and we're the best people to explain it."

Help recruiting close

Give recruiting sharper tools to tell the story, especially late in the process when someone is deciding whether to take an offer. That means a better "Why Valon" deck, candidate FAQs and offer-stage materials, pitch materials for specific roles, and straight answers to the doubts candidates actually raise. You'll learn what excites candidates, where they hesitate, and what gets them to yes.

Decide what's worth sharing

A lot happens inside Valon, and part of the job is judgment about which of it the outside world should see, and in what form. You'll spot the moments, people, and proof points worth writing about, decide whether something is a founder post, a candidate asset, or a longer piece, and protect the signal. Not everything needs to be published.

Build a system that lasts

We don't want the occasional good post. We want a repeatable way to find and tell stories: pulling ideas out of founders and teams, interviewing people and catching good stories early, turning milestones into something worth reading, publishing on a regular cadence without heavy process, and tracking what's actually moving candidates.

Who you are

You're a strong writer with good taste and sharp judgment. You could be a fit if:

  • You're constitutionally incapable of letting a good story go untold. When something happens, you're already drafting it in your head and thinking about who needs to read it.

  • You understand that a career decision is an identity decision, and you write to that.

  • You're genuinely moved by what Valon is doing: a small, serious team rebuilding the financial infrastructure the American dream depends on. If that lands flat, this isn't the right fit.

  • You can write in someone else's voice and make it sound like them.

  • You work across mediums yourself, and you can make complicated things clear without making them simplistic.

  • You've been the primary or founding brand or editorial voice somewhere, and you can point to results. Engineers shared your work. Candidates applied because of it.

  • You're writing the playbook, not executing one. There's no template for this. Stripe figured it out their way. Anduril figured out theirs. We'll figure out ours, and you're the one figuring it out.

  • You measure the right things. Offer accept rates and pipeline, not reach and impressions.

You might come from brand or content at a consumer company that got identity right, from journalism or entertainment, from founder communications, or from a writing-heavy operator role. The background matters less than whether you can find the real story and make people care.

What this role is not

  • An agency or consulting seat with no real in-house ownership.

  • A chase for viral moments. We're playing a long game, and this person needs to believe in that.

  • A job for someone who needs to be out front. Much of the best work here goes uncredited.

  • A brand strategist who "manages vendors" and hands the actual writing to someone else.

Level & Compensation

Staff IC to Director, probably 6 to 10 years in, and someone who has been the primary or founding voice somewhere rather than one writer on a large team. Comp is likely $200–260K, with room to adjust for the right person.

Location

This role is based in New York City. We use in-person time as a tool for speed, trust, and building a shared sense of what Valon's story is, which matters even more for a role this close to the founders and the rest of the company. Expect to be in the NYC office regularly. We don't manage this with rigid attendance rules; we trust you to use judgment about where the work gets done best, and to show up in person for the work that needs it.

Engineering at Valon

Our engineering team powers a modern software ecosystem designed to disrupt one of the most outdated and heavily regulated industries in finance: mortgage servicing. We’ve built the foundation of a scalable platform capable of managing billions in assets with precision and reliability. Now we’re focused on scaling infrastructure, improving developer experience, and building high-leverage systems that support rapid product iteration and long-term business growth. We’re a tight-knit, high-agency group of engineers from Stripe, Jane Street, Meta, and Google, and we aim to do the best work of our lives—together.

Our headquarters are in New York City, with a new San Francisco office opening this year. We also fully support remote work.

About the Role

We’re looking for an EM or Senior Engineering Manager to lead our Cloud Infrastructure efforts on the Platform team. In this role, you’ll manage and grow a high-impact team responsible for the foundational infrastructure powering all of Valon’s products. You’ll work across all our production systems (compute, databases, storage, and networking)—ensuring our platform is scalable, secure, and reliable. We handle over 100mm background jobs per day and expect to scale >10x over the next 2 years. Some example projects on the roadmap:

  • Adopt new data stores that support our growth: Vitess, Clickhouse, Redis.

  • Scale our batch processing control plane for faster component creation and fulfillment.

  • Production-equivalent sandbox environment for customer testing, demos, etc.

You’ll operate with a product management mindset, balancing near-term priorities with long-term platform vision. You’ll partner closely with engineering, product, and operations to define and deliver cross-cutting infrastructure initiatives. This is a hands-on leadership role—you’ll guide architecture decisions, write code when needed, and deeply understand how our systems work. You'll also be a people-first leader, focused on recruiting, coaching, giving feedback, and helping engineers thrive through 360° feedback and continuous development.

Responsibilities

  • Lead a team of 5+ engineers focused on infrastructure and platform tooling.

  • Own technical strategy, planning, and execution for core platform initiatives, with an emphasis on scalability, reliability, and security.

  • Act as a strong technical mentor and hands-on contributor when needed—guiding architecture, writing code, and debugging systems.

  • Collaborate with stakeholders across engineering, product, and operations to build infrastructure that unlocks product innovation and operational excellence.

  • Establish and evolve engineering processes for continuous improvement, velocity, and quality.

  • Invest in recruiting and developing engineering talent through coaching, mentorship, and ongoing feedback (including 360 feedback).

  • Promote a high-agency, high-accountability team culture with a bias for action and clear communication.

  • Advocate for technical excellence and pragmatic decision-making, grounded in deep system knowledge.

Ideal Background

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 1+ years in a tech lead or engineering management role.

  • Experience working on infrastructure, platform engineering, DevOps, or cloud systems.

  • Strong systems thinking and understanding of how backend and infrastructure layers interact.

  • Track record of leading teams in fast-paced, high-growth environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and grow engineers while fostering a high-performance, feedback-driven team culture.

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to align cross-functional partners around platform strategy.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud providers (e.g., AWS, GCP), containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and distributed systems.

  • A strong product mindset and the ability to translate business problems into scalable technical solutions.

Benefits

  • Compensation: competitive salary with a meaningful stake in the company via equity, and 401(k) plan. The base salary range reflects multiple levels. We assess level based on a combination of experience and interview performance.

  • Health & well-being: we’ll invest in your physical and mental well-being with comprehensive medical, dental, & vision benefits.

  • Free Food: daily lunch, and dinner provided through Forkable for in-office team members.

  • Commuter benefits: pre-tax deductions for public transit, rideshares, and parking to simplify your daily commute.

  • Grow together: company wide orientation for you to successfully onboard and other learning & development opportunities including regular review cycles that feature 360-degree feedback.

  • Play together: quarterly budgets for team and company outings. Use it for team swag, cooking classes, or team dinners.

  • Generous time off: flexible paid time off with no annual limit, sick days, and 11 company holidays.

  • Baby bonding time: 12 weeks of fully paid leave for both birthing and non-birthing parents, so you can spend uninterrupted time welcoming and caring for your newest family member.

We engage with external security auditors, pentesting firms, and partners to continuously evaluate Valon’s security posture.

In this role, you'll own the design, implementation, and operation of IAM systems for Valon’s enterprise identity stack that powers Valon's workforce, and support security for customer-facing authentication and authorization capabilities embedded in ValonOS. You'll be the connective tissue between IT, Engineering, and Security — ensuring every identity, human or machine, is governed consistently and securely.

Responsibilities

The complicated delinquent states often come with various edge case considerations; you will need to be comfortable working in ambiguity and partner with internal stakeholders to distill such complexity into simple solutions.   • Think and design at a system level. Not just at a feature level. While solving a specific problem, you consider how it relates to similar issues in other areas and how to build consistent experience.

  • User empathy and advocacy. 

  • Strong communication and collaboration. 

  • Critical thinker and thought partners. 

  • Humble and growth-oriented mindset. 

  • Caring about the big picture as much as the pixel-perfect work. 

  • Excitement about working in a startup environment.

  • 5+ years of experience with user-centered product design

  • A solid portfolio 

  • Experience working within the context of digital products

  • Ability to balance methodological rigor with scrappiness and creativity

Valon offices are located in New York City and San Francisco, but we fully support remote work!

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and skilled Senior Security Engineer, Threat & Offensive Security to join our growing team! As a key security member at Valon, you will help scale and strengthen our offensive security and threat operations, proactively identifying weaknesses in our systems, networks, and applications as the company continues to grow.

This position requires a deep understanding of adversarial techniques, security testing methodologies, threat intelligence, and incident response, along with the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams. Importantly, this role requires an AI and automation-first approach to security work, using modern tools to scale testing, threat management, and response.   • Strong understanding of common attack techniques, exploitation methods, and MITRE ATT&CK or related

  • Experience with SIEM, EDR, and other detection/monitoring platforms

  • Experience with cloud security and environments (GCP, AWS)

About the role

Be the People Partner for the teams that make Valon work: the ones deploying ValonOS, the ones selling it, and the ones running the company behind them.

You will be a trusted partner to leaders across Deployment and Implementation and the builder & owner of a People Programs roadmap for this group. You will help leaders make better decisions about organization design, workforce planning, manager effectiveness, performance, talent, and change—and then turn recurring needs into programs, tools, and operating rhythms that work in practice. This role sits at the intersection of strategic partnership and program building: you will advise Deployment and Implementation leaders while creating the manager and talent practices the organization needs next.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move between a senior leader conversation, a manager coaching session, and the details of shipping a program. You will work closely with the People team along with key stakeholders within Deployment and G&A.

Why this role matters

Most People Partner roles tune an organization that is already stable. This one asks you to help build the organization while it is running.

Our Deployment teams migrate decades-old regulated operations onto ValonOS. One client called it “open-heart surgery while the patient is still walking around.” Timelines are tight, executives are watching, and many of the managers leading the work are managing for the first time. GTM is growing beyond founder-led sales. G&A supports a company whose business model is changing in real time.

That creates people problems that keep repeating: roles that need redefining after a reorg, managers who need better tools for feedback and delegation, talent decisions that need a consistent process. Your job is to spot the patterns and turn them into programs and operating rhythms that scale. The work sits close to company strategy, is visible to the executives you partner with, and lets you point to exactly what changed because of it.

What you’ll do

Partner with Deployment and Implementation leaders

  • Advise leaders on team structure, role clarity, spans and layers, workforce planning, headcount, and growth.

  • Help leaders navigate reorganizations, operating-model changes, and the periods of re-onboarding and clarification that follow them.

  • Bring a clear point of view on manager effectiveness, team health, retention, and talent risks.

  • Translate business plans and operating challenges into practical people decisions.

Build manager capability and learning programs

  • Create and improve a manager-development program that helps managers delegate, give feedback, manage performance, develop people, and lead through change.

  • Build a practical learning and development roadmap for Deployment and Implementation, including manager learning, role-specific development, and career growth.

  • Equip managers with playbooks, tools, training, and recurring forums they will actually use.

  • Coach managers and leaders directly on difficult people and leadership situations.

Own the People Programs roadmap

  • Own the annual and quarterly roadmap for manager capability, learning and development, performance and talent practices, and organizational change support for the client group.

  • Strengthen performance management, talent reviews, development planning, promotion readiness, and succession thinking.

  • Turn recurring employee or manager challenges into scalable programs, templates, and operating rhythms.

  • Build regular listening loops with employees and managers; synthesize feedback and organizational data into clear themes, prioritized actions, and program improvements.

  • Measure whether programs are improving manager effectiveness, development, retention, engagement, and team health; use the evidence to iterate.

Own employee relations for the client group

  • Independently manage employee-relations matters from intake through resolution, including performance and conduct concerns, workplace conflict, and policy interpretation.

  • Lead investigations and make sound, timely recommendations, partnering with Legal or People leadership on sensitive or high-risk cases.

  • Coach managers through difficult conversations and documentation, ensuring fair and consistent outcomes.

Operate as a senior member of the People team

  • Partner with People Operations, People Relations, Talent Acquisition, and Legal on programs and complex situations.

  • Bring structure and judgment to ambiguous, high-stakes, and fast-moving work.

  • Make evidence-based people decisions: use employee feedback and organizational data to identify patterns, prioritize work, and communicate tradeoffs.

  • Help the People team build a consistent, high-quality experience for leaders and employees as Valon grows.

What success looks like in the first year

  • Deployment and Implementation leaders see you as a trusted, high-judgment partner.

  • The group has a clear People Programs roadmap with visible ownership, priorities, and measures.

  • Managers have stronger tools and habits for feedback, performance, delegation, development, and leading through change.

  • A practical learning and development approach is in place and being used.

  • Reorganizations and operating-model changes are supported with clearer role definition, communication, and re-onboarding.

  • Performance and talent practices are more consistent and useful to leaders and employees.

  • You can show what changed, what worked, and where the next investment should go.

What we’re looking for

  • 8+ years of experience in an HRBP, People Partner, or equivalent role, with meaningful experience advising senior leaders and executives.

  • Experience supporting an operationally complex organization such as deployment, implementation, professional services, operations, or a similarly cross-functional environment.

  • A track record of building and shipping people programs, especially manager development, learning and development, performance, talent, or organizational change programs.

  • Strong judgment and comfort operating in ambiguity, with the ability to move from strategy to execution without losing the thread.

  • Excellent manager-coaching skills and the ability to earn trust while being direct about hard issues.

  • Hands-on experience independently managing employee-relations matters, including investigations, performance and conduct issues, and manager coaching.

  • Experience with organization design, workforce planning, performance management, talent reviews, and change management.

  • Synthesize people data, employee and manager feedback, and business context to diagnose root causes, recommend targeted action, and measure impact.

  • An AI-forward mindset and practical fluency with AI tools; able to identify where AI can improve People programs, manager enablement, and team workflows while protecting confidential employee information and keeping human judgment central.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, discretion, and empathy.

  • Willingness to work in person with the team in New York City.

Mortgage or financial-services experience is helpful, but not required. You do need to learn a complex business quickly and care about how the work gets done.

Benefits

  • Compensation: competitive base salary range of $180K-$225K with a meaningful stake in the company via equity, and 401k plan.

Employee lifecycle operations

  • Own onboarding from signed offer through a smooth new-hire experience.

  • Ensure employee data, documentation, and cross-functional handoffs are accurate and timely.

  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, integrations, and self-service.

  • Maintain accurate records and audit-ready documentation.

  • Own day-to-day benefits administration, employee support, and vendor coordination.

  • Support renewals, open enrollment, plan changes, and ongoing benefits communications.

  • Coordinate leave-related processes and ensure employees receive timely, accurate guidance.

  • Partner with Total Rewards and external providers to resolve issues and improve the employee experience.

  • Manage workers’ compensation coverage, renewals, audits, and claims coordination with brokers, carriers, and internal partners.

Immigration and work authorization

  • Coordinate immigration and work authorization processes with employees, outside counsel, and relevant vendors.

  • Track cases, deadlines, documentation, and employee communications.

  • Ensure processes are organized, timely, and handled with appropriate confidentiality.

  • Escalate legal questions to Legal or outside counsel rather than providing legal advice.

  • Balance roadmap execution with day-to-day operations, ensuring clear priorities and reliable coverage.

  • Stay close enough to the work to handle complex issues and model excellent execution.

  • Build and maintain automations using no-code, low-code, workflow, and AI tools.
